title: CRPS-stacked ensemble weights — crps_weights
text: R wrapper mirrors `lopensemble::crps_weights`. Optimises weights softmax space empirical mixture-CRPS objective Dirichlet log-prior penalty.

title: CRPS-stacked ensemble weights — crps_weights
text: training data frame columns `model_id`, `output_type` (must `"sample"`), `output_type_id` (sample index), `value`, plus task-id columns. observations data frame task-id columns plus column named exactly `observed`. task_id_cols Character vector column names identify forecast task, e.g. `"date"` `c("location", "date")`. dirichlet_alpha Concentration Dirichlet log-prior penalty weights. Values just 1 (default 1.001, matching `lopensemble`) give almost flat prior whose effect keep optimum simplex boundary; larger values pull weights toward uniformity, strength decaying number training tasks grows.

title: CRPS-stacked ensemble weights — crps_weights
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ set.seed(1) n_samples <- 100 n_task <- 30 y <- rnorm(n_task)  make_samples <- function(model_id, sampler) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_task), function(t) data.frame(     model_id = model_id, output_type = "sample",     output_type_id = seq_len(n_samples),     t = t, value = sampler(y[t]),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ))) } train <- rbind(   make_samples("m_good",  function(yt) yt + rnorm(n_samples, sd = 0.4)),   make_samples("m_noisy", function(yt) rnorm(n_samples, sd = 3)) ) obs <- data.frame(t = seq_len(n_task), observed = y) crps_weights(train, obs, task_id_cols = "t") } # }

title: Quantile Regression Averaging — qra
text: training data frame columns `model_id`, `output_type` (must `"quantile"`), `output_type_id`, `value`, plus task-id columns. target data frame shape: forecasts combine using fitted weights. observations data frame task-id columns plus column named exactly `observed`. task_id_cols Character vector column names identify forecast task, e.g. `c("location", "horizon", "target_date")`. per_quantile_weights TRUE, fit separate weights per quantile. intercept Include intercept term regression. enforce_normalisation Constrain weights lie simplex. noncross Add cross-quantile monotonicity constraints. takes effect `per_quantile_weights = TRUE`; silently without effect otherwise (joint fit cross construction `enforce_normalisation = TRUE`). group Character vector task dimensions fit separate regressions (e.g. `"location"` per-location weights). title: Quantile Regression Averaging — qra
text: `qrensemble::qra` takes single `forecast_quantile` object containing training holdout rows plus `target` filter; function takes three explicit data frames. convert: rename `model` `model_id`, `quantile_level` `output_type_id` `predicted` `value`; add `output_type = "quantile"` column; split rows `training` `target` (e.g. `target_date`); put observed values separate `observations` frame task-id columns plus column named exactly `observed`. defaults (`per_quantile_weights = FALSE`, `enforce_normalisation = TRUE`, `intercept = FALSE`, `noncross = TRUE`) match `qrensemble::qra`, tuned call carries unchanged.

title: Quantile Regression Averaging — qra
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # 50 training points, 1 holdout, 2 component models, 5 quantile levels. set.seed(1) taus <- c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9) n <- 50 y <- rnorm(n + 1) make_rows <- function(model_id, predictions) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(taus, function(q) data.frame(     model_id = model_id, output_type = "quantile",     output_type_id = q, t = seq_along(predictions),     value = predictions + qnorm(q),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ))) } rows <- rbind(   make_rows("m_good",  y + 0.3 * rnorm(n + 1)),   make_rows("m_noisy", 2 * rnorm(n + 1)) ) train  <- rows[rows$t <= n, ]    # tasks 1..50 train target <- rows[rows$t == n + 1, ] # task 51 is the holdout obs <- data.frame(t = seq_len(n), observed = y[seq_len(n)])  result <- qra(training = train, target = target, observations = obs,               task_id_cols = "t") attr(result, "weights") } # }

title: ensembles 0.1.0
text: Initial release. Mirrors user-facing API hubEnsembles (simple_ensemble(), linear_pool()), qrensemble (qra()), lopensemble (crps_weights(), mixture_from_samples()), delegating numerics Julia package Ensembles.jl JuliaConnectoR bridge. Differences packages mirrors: task_id_cols required argument throughout (hub schema assumed). linear_pool() names sample-count argument n_samples (n_output_samples hubEnsembles) computes quantile-input ensembles exactly, Monte Carlo step. qra() takes three explicit data frames (training, target, observations) rather qrensemble’s single filtered forecast object; fitted weights attached result attr(result, "weights"). crps_weights() expects hubverse column vocabulary (model_id, output_type_id, value) observations separate frame; lambda time-weighting argument lopensemble yet supported. Outputs carry model_out_tbl class; ensemble model_id configurable via model_id argument. Stochastic operations (sample-input pooling) accept seed argument; R’s set.seed() reach Julia process.
